docs.title: MySQLTuner Documentation
docs.text:
Current Version: 2.9.4

MySQLTuner is a single-file Perl diagnostic and performance tuning advisor for MySQL, MariaDB, and Percona Server. It runs with zero non-core CPAN dependencies, evaluates over 900 indicators, and computes a Weighted Health Score (0-100) across Performance, Security, and Resilience. It also integrates with AI workflows through --agent-json, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and curated domain skills.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Welcome to the MySQLTuner learning lab! These step-by-step tutorials teach you how to run database diagnostics and AI-assisted audits safely inside isolated local Docker sandboxes before touching any shared environment.

Environment Warning: Execute tutorial commands only against disposable local Docker containers. Never point sandbox commands at staging or production databases.

docs.title: Available Labs
docs.text:
1. First Audit Sandbox: Start a local MariaDB container, run a verbose CLI audit, inspect the Weighted Health Score, and generate a standalone HTML diagnostic dashboard.
  2. AI & MCP Sandbox Lab: Export actionable --agent-json telemetry, inspect the offline --list-indicators catalog, and interact with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over JSON-RPC stdio.

docs.title: Tutorial: First MySQLTuner Audit Sandbox
docs.text:
Learning Goal: Spin up a disposable MariaDB container, run a full verbose MySQLTuner audit, generate a standalone HTML dashboard report, and clean up the sandbox cleanly.

Environment Warning: Run this tutorial only in an isolated local Docker sandbox. Never run tutorial commands against staging or production database servers.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Make sure your workstation has the following tools ready before starting:

  • Docker Engine 24+ (or compatible container runtime)
  • Perl 5.6+ (core modules only; no CPAN installs required)
  • MySQL or MariaDB command-line client (mysql or mariadb)
  • Local repository checkout of MySQLTuner-perl
  • Local TCP port 13306 available

docs.title: What You Will Accomplish
docs.text:
By the end of this tutorial, you will have:

  1. Launched an isolated MariaDB 11.4 sandbox container on port 13306.
  2. Executed perl mysqltuner.pl --verbose to inspect storage engines, health score, and recommendations.
  3. Generated a self-contained HTML diagnostic report using --reportfile.
  4. Audited the container directly via --container and removed the sandbox cleanly.

docs.title: Sandbox Workflow Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Start["1. Start MariaDB Container"] --> Verbose["2. Run Verbose Audit"]
    Verbose --> Report["3. Generate HTML Report"]
    Report --> Container["4. Inspect Container Metrics"]
    Container --> Cleanup["5. Remove Sandbox"]

docs.title: Step 1: Start an Isolated MariaDB Sandbox
docs.text:
Launch a temporary MariaDB 11.4 container with a sandbox password and wait until it accepts queries:

docker run -d \
  --name mt-sandbox-db \
  -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=sandbox_pass \
  -p 13306:3306 \
  mariadb:11.4

Verify that the database responds inside the container:

docker exec mt-sandbox-db mariadb -uroot -psandbox_pass \
  -e "SELECT VERSION() AS mariadb_version, @@port AS port;"

Expected output:

+--------------------+------+
| mariadb_version    | port |
+--------------------+------+
| 11.4.x-MariaDB-... | 3306 |
+--------------------+------+
1 row in set (0.001 sec)

docs.title: Step 2: Run Your First Verbose Audit
docs.text:
Execute mysqltuner.pl from the repository root with --verbose and --forcemem so MySQLTuner knows the simulated host RAM allocation for accurate buffer recommendations:

perl mysqltuner.pl \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 13306 \
  --user root \
  --pass sandbox_pass \
  --forcemem 4G \
  --verbose

Expected output (abbreviated):

 >>  MySQLTuner 2.9.4
         * Jean-Marie Renouard <jmrenouard@gmail.com>
         * Major Hayden <major@mhtx.net>
 >>  Bug reports, feature requests, and downloads at http://mysqltuner.pl/
 >>  Run with '--help' for additional options and output filtering

-------- Storage Engine Statistics -----------------------------------------------------------------
[--] Status: +Aria +CSV +InnoDB +MEMORY +MyISAM +SEQUENCE
[--] Data in InnoDB tables: 0B (Tables: 0)
...
-------- Health Score KPI --------------------------------------------------------------------------
Overall Weighted Health Score: 75/100
    - Performance: 25/40
    - Security:    20/30
    - Resilience:  30/30
[--] Your database health is good, but there's room for improvement.

-------- Recommendations ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
General recommendations:
    MySQL started within last 24 hours - recommendations may be inaccurate
    Performance_schema should be activated.

Notice two helpful things right away: MySQLTuner flags when uptime is under 24 hours, and it summarizes a Weighted Health Score out of 100 across Performance, Security, and Resilience.

docs.title: Step 3: Generate a Standalone HTML Report
docs.text:
MySQLTuner builds an interactive HTML dashboard in pure Perl with zero external dependencies. Run the audit again with --reportfile to save a self-contained report:

perl mysqltuner.pl \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 13306 \
  --user root \
  --pass sandbox_pass \
  --forcemem 4G \
  --reportfile /tmp/sandbox_report.html

Verify that MySQLTuner created the HTML file:

ls -lh /tmp/sandbox_report.html

Expected output:

-rw-r--r-- 1 user user 42K Nov 23 12:00 /tmp/sandbox_report.html

Open /tmp/sandbox_report.html in any browser to view the Health Score gauge, category breakdowns, and collapsible console output.

docs.title: Step 4: Audit the Container Directly with --container
docs.text:
Instead of passing host RAM manually, pass --container to let MySQLTuner inspect cgroup memory limits and container logs directly through Docker:

perl mysqltuner.pl \
  --container docker:mt-sandbox-db \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 13306 \
  --user root \
  --pass sandbox_pass \
  --verbose

In container mode, MySQLTuner automatically skips host kernel recommendations (sysctl) that do not apply inside an isolated container.

docs.title: Step 5: Clean Up the Sandbox
docs.text:
Remove the temporary container and generated report file once you finish exploring:

docker rm -f mt-sandbox-db
rm -f /tmp/sandbox_report.html

Expected output:

mt-sandbox-db

docs.title: Tutorial: AI Agent & MCP Sandbox Lab
docs.text:
Learning Goal: Produce machine-readable --agent-json remediation plans, export the offline indicator catalog, and interact with the MySQLTuner Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in an isolated local Docker sandbox.

Environment Warning: Keep READ_ONLY=true during learning sessions and run all commands only against a disposable local Docker container. Never connect AI write tools to production servers during a tutorial.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Ensure your local environment includes:

  • Docker Engine 24+
  • Python 3.8+ (standard library only; zero external pip packages required for build/mcp_server.py)
  • Perl 5.6+ with JSON::PP (included in Perl core since 5.14)
  • Local repository checkout of MySQLTuner-perl
  • Local TCP port 13306 available

docs.title: What You Will Accomplish
docs.text:
By the end of this lab, you will have:

  1. Inspected MySQLTuner's offline indicator catalog with --list-indicators.
  2. Launched a temporary MariaDB 11.4 container and extracted actionable fixes via --agent-json.
  3. Built the containerized MCP server image from Dockerfile.mcp.
  4. Sent JSON-RPC 2.0 initialize, tools/list, and tools/call requests to build/mcp_server.py over stdio.

docs.title: Lab Execution Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Ind["1. Export Indicators (--list-indicators)"] --> DB["2. Start MariaDB Container"]
    DB --> Agent["3. Collect --agent-json"]
    Agent --> Img["4. Build Dockerfile.mcp"]
    Img --> RPC["5. Query mcp_server.py stdio"]
    RPC --> Clean["6. Clean Up Sandbox"]

docs.title: Step 1: Export the Offline Indicator Catalog
docs.text:
Before starting a database, test offline indicator discovery. This flag needs no database connection:

perl mysqltuner.pl --list-indicators | head -n 25

Expected output:

{
   "cli_options" : {
      "agent-json" : {
         "cat" : "PERFORMANCE",
         "default" : 0,
         "desc" : "Print result as actionable JSON schema for AI agents",
         "placeholder" : null,
         "type" : "!"
      },

docs.title: Step 2: Start the Sandbox Database and Collect --agent-json
docs.text:
Start a disposable MariaDB 11.4 container on port 13306:

docker run -d \
  --name mt-mcp-sandbox \
  -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=sandbox_pass \
  -p 13306:3306 \
  mariadb:11.4

Wait until the server accepts queries, then run mysqltuner.pl with --agent-json:

perl mysqltuner.pl \
  --agent-json \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 13306 \
  --user root \
  --pass sandbox_pass \
  --forcemem 4G

Expected output (abbreviated JSON structure):

{
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "performance_schema_enable",
      "topic": "Performance",
      "description": "Performance Schema is disabled.",
      "impact_score": 8,
      "risk_level": "Medium",
      "requires_restart": true,
      "action": {
        "type": "Config",
        "statement": "performance_schema = ON",
        "rollback_statement": "performance_schema = OFF"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Every finding includes impact_score, risk_level, requires_restart, and a matching rollback_statement so AI agents can evaluate safety before proposing any change.

docs.title: Step 3: Build the Dockerfile.mcp Microservice Image
docs.text:
Inspect Dockerfile.mcp and build a local mysqltuner-mcp image from the repository root:

docker build -f Dockerfile.mcp -t mysqltuner-mcp .

Expected output (final lines):

=> exporting to image
=> => naming to docker.io/library/mysqltuner-mcp:latest

docs.title: Step 4: Query build/mcp_server.py Over JSON-RPC Stdio
docs.text:
Run build/mcp_server.py locally in safe READ_ONLY=true mode against your sandbox database and send three JSON-RPC requests over standard input:

mkdir -p /tmp/mt-mcp-cache
printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":2}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","id":3,"params":{"name":"analyze_buffer_pool","arguments":{"target_ram_percentage":75}}}' \
| DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT=13306 DB_USER=root DB_PASSWORD=sandbox_pass \
  CACHE_DIR=/tmp/mt-mcp-cache READ_ONLY=true MYSQLTUNER_PL=./mysqltuner.pl \
  python3 build/mcp_server.py

Expected output (three JSON-RPC response lines):

{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "capabilities": {"tools": {}, "resources": {}, "prompts": {}}, "serverInfo": {"name": "mysqltuner-mcp", "version": "2.9.4"}}, "id": 1}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"tools": [{"name": "get_latest_audit", ...}, {"name": "run_audit", ...}, {"name": "analyze_buffer_pool", ...}, {"name": "diagnose_replication_lag", ...}, {"name": "detect_fragmented_tables", ...}, {"name": "apply_recommendation", ...}, {"name": "rollback_recommendation", ...}]}, "id": 2}
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "{\n  \"status\": \"OPTIMAL\",\n  \"metrics\": {\n    \"hit_ratio_pct\": 100.0,\n..."}]}]}, "id": 3}

With READ_ONLY=true, diagnostic tools (run_audit, get_latest_audit, analyze_buffer_pool, diagnose_replication_lag, detect_fragmented_tables) succeed while write tools (apply_recommendation, rollback_recommendation) safely refuse execution.

docs.title: Step 5: Clean Up the Sandbox
docs.text:
Remove the temporary container and MCP cache directory:

docker rm -f mt-mcp-sandbox
rm -rf /tmp/mt-mcp-cache

docs.title: Publish Versioned Documentation
docs.text: Refer to Release Notes Archive for current release versions before you start this procedure.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before you start this procedure, make sure that these conditions apply:

  1. Python 3.8 or a newer version and Git exist on your workstation.
  2. You have markdownlint-cli2 on your workstation if you execute local lint checks.
  3. For manual GitHub Actions deployment, you have repository write access and IONOS SFTP secrets.

docs.title: Safety Precautions
docs.text:
CAUTION: Run make docs-check and mkdocs build --strict before you publish a version. Broken relative links or incorrect mike aliases break documentation navigation.

NOTE: The mkdocs.yml file sets mike to alias_type: redirect for a static Apache web server.

docs.title: Step 1: Install Documentation Dependencies
docs.text:
1. Create a virtual environment and install the documentation packages:
make docs-install

docs.title: Step 2: Validate Structure, STE Compliance, and Strict Build
docs.text:
1. Run the Diataxis structure and link check in strict mode:
make docs-check
  1. Run markdownlint-cli2 across all Markdown pages:
npx markdownlint-cli2 "docs/**/*.md"
  1. Run the strict MkDocs build to validate hooks, release injection, and navigation:
make docs-build

docs.title: Step 3: Preview Locally
docs.text:
1. Start the local preview server and examine changes in your browser:
make docs-serve
  1. Stop the preview server with Ctrl+C when your examination finishes.

docs.title: Option A: Publish via GitHub Actions
docs.text:
1. Open the GitHub Actions tab and select .github/workflows/docs-deploy.yml.

  2. Start workflow_dispatch with target version (for example 2.9.4), alias (latest), and set_default.

  3. Set dry_run to true for a rehearsal, or set false to push docs-site and upload to IONOS.

docs.title: Option B: Deploy Manually with mike
docs.text:
1. Fetch the docs-site branch from origin and build the new versioned directory:
git fetch origin docs-site:docs-site || true
mike deploy --branch docs-site --update-aliases 2.9.4 latest
mike set-default --branch docs-site latest
  1. Preview the versioned mike site locally before you push:
mike serve --branch docs-site
  1. Push the docs-site branch to origin:
git push origin docs-site

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. Make sure that make docs-check and make docs-build exit with code 0.

  2. Examine versions.json on docs-site and make sure that the new version and latest alias exist:

git show docs-site:versions.json
  1. Open the site URL and make sure that the version selector switches between versions cleanly.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
If an active documentation version contains errors, restore the previous version alias immediately:

  1. Delete the broken version directory from the docs-site branch:
mike delete --branch docs-site 2.9.4
  1. Point the latest alias back to the previous healthy version (for example 2.9.3):
mike deploy --branch docs-site --update-aliases 2.9.3 latest
mike set-default --branch docs-site latest
git push origin docs-site
  1. Run .github/workflows/docs-deploy.yml again with workflow_dispatch to synchronize the static IONOS host.

docs.title: Run Remote and Container Audits
docs.text: Refer to CLI Options and Environment before you start this procedure.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before you start this procedure, make sure that these conditions apply:

  1. You have database access credentials with read privileges on the target server.
  2. Perl 5.6 or a newer version exists on the control host.
  3. For SSH mode, SSH key access or sshpass exists on the control host.
  4. For container mode, the docker, podman, or kubectl CLI exists on the control host.

docs.title: Safety Precautions
docs.text:
CAUTION: Never put passwords in plain CLI arguments on shared hosts. Other users can read command arguments from process lists.

NOTE: Container mode probes cgroup memory limits and skips host kernel checks.

docs.title: Method A: Audit via SSH Transport
docs.text:
1. Set database and SSH parameters, then start mysqltuner.pl with --ssh-host:
perl mysqltuner.pl \
  --ssh-host db01.internal \
  --ssh-user dba_ops \
  --ssh-identity-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
  --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf \
  --verbose

  1. If the target uses an SSH password instead of a key, install sshpass first.

  2. Pass --ssh-password only in an isolated automation runner, not on shared terminals.

docs.title: Method B: Audit via Direct Remote TCP
docs.text:
1. Get the physical RAM and swap totals from the server administrator.

  2. Set --forcemem and --forceswap so buffer calculations match the remote server hardware:

export MYSQL_PWD_USER="mysqltuner"
export MYSQL_PWD_VAL="secret"
perl mysqltuner.pl \
  --host 192.0.2.50 \
  --port 3306 \
  --userenv MYSQL_PWD_USER \
  --passenv MYSQL_PWD_VAL \
  --forcemem 32G \
  --forceswap 4G \
  --verbose
  1. If you audit a managed cloud database without SSH, add --cloud (and --azure on Azure).

NOTE: Direct --cloud mode without --ssh-host assumes 1024 MB RAM unless you pass --forcemem.

docs.title: Method C: Audit Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes Containers
docs.text:
1. Run mysqltuner.pl with --container and the runtime prefix (docker:, podman:, or kubectl:):
# Docker container
perl mysqltuner.pl --container docker:prod_mysql --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf --verbose

# Podman container
perl mysqltuner.pl --container podman:prod_mariadb --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf --verbose

# Kubernetes pod
perl mysqltuner.pl --container kubectl:mysql-primary-0 --host 127.0.0.1 --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf --verbose
  1. Examine the cgroup memory limit and container error log summary in the terminal output.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. Examine the header output and make sure that the target hostname or container name appears.

  2. Make sure that the System Linux Recommendations or cgroup memory lines show accurate RAM values.

  3. Make sure that no SSH or container transport errors appear in the output.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
This audit executes read-only commands and makes no server changes.

  1. If a temporary SSH agent or terminal session stays open, close the session.

  2. Remove temporary report files or credentials files from /tmp after review:

rm -f /tmp/mysqltuner_report.html /tmp/result_mysqltuner.txt

docs.title: Diagnose Replication Lag
docs.text: Refer to Diagnostic Alerts Matrix for lag thresholds and alert definitions.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before you start this procedure, make sure that these conditions apply:

  1. You have database access credentials with REPLICATION CLIENT or REPLICA MONITOR privileges.
  2. You have SUPER or REPLICATION_SLAVE_ADMIN privileges if you must adjust worker threads.
  3. You know the primary source hostname and current maintenance window status.

docs.title: Safety Precautions
docs.text:
CAUTION: Never skip replication errors or reset binary log coordinates without DBA authorization. Incorrect position resets cause permanent data divergence between primary and replica nodes.

NOTE: MySQL 8.0.22+ and MariaDB 10.5+ use REPLICA syntax, while older versions use SLAVE.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Run mysqltuner.pl on the replica node to examine topology, thread state, GTID gaps, and lag:
perl mysqltuner.pl --verbose --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf
  1. Query the replica status directly in SQL to examine exact thread fields and errors:
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G
-- On MySQL < 8.0.22 or MariaDB < 10.5:
SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G

  1. Examine Replica_IO_Running and Replica_SQL_Running (or Slave_IO_Running and Slave_SQL_Running).

  2. If either thread shows No, examine Last_IO_Error, Last_SQL_Error, and Last_SQL_Errno immediately.

  3. Fix network or privilege failures for IO thread errors before you run START REPLICA;.

  4. If the two threads show Yes and Seconds_Behind_Source climbs, examine the worker count:

-- MySQL 8.0+
SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'replica_parallel_workers';
-- MariaDB 10.5+
SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('slave_parallel_threads', 'slave_parallel_mode');

  1. Record the current worker count and mode before you make a change.

  2. If parallel worker threads equal 0 or 1, stop the SQL thread and increase worker concurrency:

-- MySQL 8.0+ example
STOP REPLICA SQL_THREAD;
SET GLOBAL replica_parallel_workers = 4;
START REPLICA SQL_THREAD;
  1. On MariaDB 10.5 or newer, set slave_parallel_threads and slave_parallel_mode = 'optimistic':
STOP SLAVE SQL_THREAD;
SET GLOBAL slave_parallel_threads = 4;
SET GLOBAL slave_parallel_mode = 'optimistic';
START SLAVE SQL_THREAD;
  1. Examine binlog_format on the primary source and make sure that ROW format is active.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. Run SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G (or SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G) and make sure that the two threads show Yes.

  2. Monitor Seconds_Behind_Source (or Seconds_Behind_Master) across three checks and make sure that lag drops.

  3. Run mysqltuner.pl --verbose and make sure that no GTID gap or thread alert remains.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
If worker concurrency triggers lock contention or replication errors, revert to the previous thread values:

  1. Stop the replica SQL thread safely:
STOP REPLICA SQL_THREAD;
  1. Apply the recorded baseline worker variable values:
SET GLOBAL replica_parallel_workers = <previous_count>;
  1. Start the replica SQL thread and make sure that the two threads show Yes:
START REPLICA SQL_THREAD;
SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G

docs.title: Run Offline Verification Tests
docs.text: Refer to CLI Options and Environment before you start this procedure.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before you start this procedure, make sure that these conditions apply:

  1. Perl 5.8 or a newer version exists on your workstation.
  2. Python 3.8 or a newer version and make exist on your workstation.
  3. A local checkout of MySQLTuner-perl is clean on a dedicated branch.

docs.title: Safety Precautions
docs.text:
CAUTION: Run tests inside an isolated checkout or clean branch. Never write test output files over production databases or host directories.

NOTE: The offline verification commands require zero network access and zero database containers.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Verify Perl syntax on mysqltuner.pl:
perl -c mysqltuner.pl
  1. Run mysqltuner.pl with --help and make sure that help text displays without errors:
perl mysqltuner.pl --help
  1. Export the offline JSON indicator catalog with --list-indicators:
perl mysqltuner.pl --list-indicators | head -n 20
  1. Run build/mcp_server.py with --help to verify the MCP server entrypoint:
CACHE_DIR=/tmp/mt-mcp-cache python3 build/mcp_server.py --help
  1. Run the Perl unit and compliance test suite:
make unit-tests
  1. Run the Python and Perl issue triage test suite:
make test-triage
  1. Run the Diataxis structure and STE documentation checks:
make docs-check

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. Make sure that perl -c mysqltuner.pl prints mysqltuner.pl syntax OK and exits with code 0.

  2. Make sure that make unit-tests, make test-triage, and make docs-check exit with code 0.

  3. Examine git status --short and make sure that zero temporary test artifacts remain on disk:

git status --short

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
If a check fails after local edits, revert the modified file and run the suite again:

  1. Discard broken test or documentation changes on the current branch:
git checkout -- <modified_file>
  1. Run make unit-tests and make docs-check again to confirm green status.

docs.title: Tune InnoDB Buffer Pool Safely
docs.text: Refer to Diagnostic Alerts Matrix and Thresholds and Data Files before you start.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before you start this procedure, make sure that these conditions apply:

  1. The database server has a minimum uptime of 24 hours under normal production traffic.
  2. You have SUPER or SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN privileges on the target instance.
  3. A current backup of /etc/mysql/my.cnf (or /etc/my.cnf) exists on disk.
  4. Free physical host RAM matches the planned buffer pool size without swap pressure.

docs.title: Safety Precautions
docs.text:
CAUTION: Calculate free host RAM before you increase innodb_buffer_pool_size. Excess memory allocation triggers OS swap activity or an out-of-memory process kill.

NOTE: On MariaDB 10.4 and newer, innodb_buffer_pool_instances no longer exists.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Run mysqltuner.pl with --buffers and --verbose to measure current InnoDB memory and hit ratios:
perl mysqltuner.pl --buffers --verbose --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf
  1. Record the current innodb_buffer_pool_size, innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size, and innodb_buffer_pool_instances values:
SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN (
  'innodb_buffer_pool_size',
  'innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size',
  'innodb_buffer_pool_instances'
);

  1. Calculate a target size that fits below 75% of dedicated host RAM.

  2. On MySQL, make sure that the target size equals a multiple of chunk_size * instances.

  3. Apply the new buffer pool size dynamically with SET GLOBAL:

SET GLOBAL innodb_buffer_pool_size = 4294967296;
  1. Wait until InnoDB completes the background resize operation:
SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'Innodb_buffer_pool_resize_status';
  1. Write the exact byte or gigabyte value under [mysqld] in my.cnf so restarts keep the value:
[mysqld]
innodb_buffer_pool_size = 4G
  1. If you must change innodb_buffer_pool_instances on MySQL, schedule a maintenance restart.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. Make sure that Innodb_buffer_pool_resize_status shows Completed resizing buffer pool or an empty string.

  2. Query SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'innodb_buffer_pool_size'; and make sure that the byte count matches.

  3. Run mysqltuner.pl again after workload warm-up and make sure that the hit ratio exceeds 95%:

perl mysqltuner.pl --buffers --verbose --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf
  1. Examine OS memory with free -m and make sure that zero swap growth occurs.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
If memory pressure or query latency increases after the adjustment, revert the pool size immediately:

  1. Apply the original recorded innodb_buffer_pool_size value dynamically:
SET GLOBAL innodb_buffer_pool_size = <previous_bytes>;

  1. Wait until Innodb_buffer_pool_resize_status shows completion.

  2. Replace my.cnf with the backup file on disk.

docs.title: Audit TLS and Authentication Plugins
docs.text: Refer to Diagnostic Alerts Matrix and Thresholds and Data Files before you start.

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Before you start this procedure, make sure that these conditions apply:

  1. You have administrative read access to mysql.user (or mysql.global_priv on MariaDB 10.4+).
  2. The openssl binary exists locally if you audit certificate expiration dates.
  3. You know which client drivers connect to the database server before you alter authentication plugins.

docs.title: Safety Precautions
docs.text:
CAUTION: Verify client driver compatibility before you switch user accounts to caching_sha2_password or ed25519. Older client libraries fail to connect after an incompatible plugin change.

NOTE: MySQLTuner skips SSL/TLS checks when the server accepts connections only on localhost.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Run mysqltuner.pl on TCP with --dumpdir to examine TLS parameters and export CSV findings:
perl mysqltuner.pl \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --verbose \
  --dumpdir /tmp/tls-audit \
  --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf

  1. Examine SSL/TLS Security Recommendations and Authentication Plugin Security in the output.

  2. Examine exported /tmp/tls-audit/ssl_issues.csv and /tmp/tls-audit/insecure_authentication_plugins.csv (mode 0600).

  3. If tls_version includes TLSv1 or TLSv1.1, restrict [mysqld] in my.cnf to modern protocols:

[mysqld]
tls_version = TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3
require_secure_transport = ON

  1. If ssl_cert or ssl_ca expires in less than 30 days, renew and reload the TLS certificates.

  2. For remote accounts that do not enforce SSL, enforce TLS per account:

ALTER USER 'app_user'@'10.0.%' REQUIRE SSL;
  1. For accounts that use mysql_native_password or sha256_password, migrate to modern plugins:
-- MySQL 8.0+ / 8.4+ / 9.x
ALTER USER 'app_user'@'10.0.%' IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password BY 'strong_secret';

-- MariaDB 10.4+ (ed25519) or local unix_socket
ALTER USER 'app_user'@'10.0.%' IDENTIFIED VIA ed25519 USING PASSWORD('strong_secret');

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. Run mysqltuner.pl --host 127.0.0.1 --verbose --defaults-file ~/.my.cnf again.

  2. Make sure that Only secure TLS versions enabled: TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3 and require_secure_transport is ON appear.

  3. Make sure that No users found using insecure or deprecated authentication plugins appears.

  4. Make sure that All remote users have SSL enforcement active appears in the security summary.

  5. Remove the temporary audit directory /tmp/tls-audit after your examination.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
If legacy applications fail TLS handshakes or plugin authentication, restore access immediately:

  1. If require_secure_transport = ON blocks unencrypted legacy clients temporarily, run:
SET GLOBAL require_secure_transport = OFF;

  1. Revert an affected account to its previous authentication plugin or TLS requirement on MySQL 8.0/8.4 or MariaDB.

  2. Restore the previous tls_version value in my.cnf and reload TLS if legacy clients need an interim window.

docs.text: MySQLTuner 2.9.4 - MySQL High Performance Tuning Advisor for MySQL, MariaDB, and Percona Server

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text:
mysqltuner [OPTIONS]

# Basic local execution using standard unix socket
perl mysqltuner.pl

# Remote TCP/IP connection with explicit credentials and forced memory sizing
perl mysqltuner.pl --host 192.168.1.50 --port 3306 --user root --pass secret --forcemem 16G

# Containerized database analysis via Docker/Podman
perl mysqltuner.pl --container production_mysql_1 --user root --pass secret

# Generate comprehensive interactive HTML diagnostic dashboard
perl mysqltuner.pl --reportfile /var/www/html/tuner_report.html

# Export schema markdown documentation per database
perl mysqltuner.pl --schemadir /opt/db_docs/

# AI Agent integration output (actionable JSON remediation plan)
perl mysqltuner.pl --agent-json

# Export indicator catalog and metadata in JSON format (offline, no database connection)
perl mysqltuner.pl --list-indicators

docs.title: IMPORTANT USAGE GUIDELINES
docs.text:
• Production Stability: Run the script without modifying arguments first to review recommendations before applying changes.
  • Representative Workload: Allow your database server to run under normal production load for at least 24 to 48 hours before trusting metric ratios and sizing advice.
  • Privilege Requirements: Administrative read-only access (SELECT, PROCESS, SHOW DATABASES, REPLICATION CLIENT) is required for exhaustive diagnostics.
  • Remote Host Hardware Sizing: When connecting over TCP/IP or SSH to remote instances, specify host RAM via --forcemem (e.g., --forcemem 32G) to ensure accurate buffer sizing recommendations.

docs.title: Upstream Security Policy
docs.text: MySQLTuner is committed to providing a secure and reliable experience for all users. This document outlines our security policies, supported versions, and the process for reporting vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text:
We provide security updates for the following versions of MySQLTuner:

Version Status v2.x Supported (v2.9.4) < v2.x End of Life

We strongly recommend that all users stay updated with the latest stable release available on GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
If you discover a security vulnerability in MySQLTuner, please do not open a public issue. Instead, report it privately to the maintainer:

  • Contact: Jean-Marie Renouard (jmrenouard@lightpath.fr)

docs.title: Reporting Guidelines
docs.text:
Please include the following information in your report:

  • A description of the vulnerability.
  • Steps to reproduce the issue (proof of concept).
  • Potential impact and affected versions.

docs.title: What to Expect
docs.text:
• Acknowledgement: You will receive an initial response within 48-72 hours.
  • Triage: We will investigate the report and determine the impact.
  • Resolution: We will work on a fix as a priority.
  • Disclosure: We will coordinate with you to determine a mutually agreeable disclosure timeline.

docs.title: In-Scope Vulnerabilities
docs.text:
• Local Privilege Escalation through insecure system calls.
  • Credential leaks in the report output (unless explicitly permitted via CLI options).
  • Remote Code Execution (RCE) via malicious database responses.
  • Insecure storage of temporary data.

docs.title: Out-of-Scope
docs.text:
• Vulnerabilities in the underlying Percona/MySQL/MariaDB database itself.
  • Issues requiring root access to the host machine to exploit.
  • Denial of Service (DoS) attacks that are inherent to database benchmarking or diagnostics.

docs.title: Security Philosophy
docs.text:
• Production Stability: Every recommendation is designed to be safe for production environments. No destructive actions are performed.
  • Read-Only Architecture: MySQLTuner is strictly a read-only script. It does not modify database configurations or system files.
  • Zero-Dependency Portability: To minimize the attack surface, MySQLTuner only uses Perl Core modules and avoids external dependencies.
  • CVE Detection: The script proactively checks for known CVEs based on the detected database version.
  • Auditability: As a single-file Perl script, MySQLTuner is easily auditable by security teams before deployment.

Nine specialized skill capsules in .agent/skills/ provide mathematical formulas, version-divergence guards, and operational safety boundaries:

docs.title: MCP Server Execution Model (build/mcp_server.py)
docs.text:
build/mcp_server.py implements MCP 2024-11-05 over JSON-RPC 2.0 using Python 3 standard library modules only:

  • Dual Transport: Serves stdio by default for desktop IDE clients, or HTTP Server-Sent Events (--sse) with /sse, /message, and /health endpoints. When --sse starts without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN, READ_ONLY is forced to true so unauthenticated HTTP clients cannot mutate database state.
  • Atomic Cache and Fail-Closed Queries: run_audit and the periodic daemon thread write latest.json and latest.html via temporary files and atomic os.replace(). Targeted tools (analyze_buffer_pool, diagnose_replication_lag, detect_fragmented_tables) fail closed on SQL errors instead of returning synthetic metrics.
  • SQL Sanitization and State Ledger: apply_recommendation passes SQL through sanitize_sql_statement(), which strips comments, blocks multi-statement payloads and destructive verbs, and restricts execution to an explicit command prefix allowlist. Before executing, it records @@global.<variable_name> in $CACHE_DIR/state.json so rollback_recommendation can emit an exact reverse SET GLOBAL statement.

docs.title: --agent-json Design (mysqltuner.pl)
docs.text:
For daemonless pipelines, perl mysqltuner.pl --agent-json converts @adjvars tuning recommendations into structured JSON findings:

  • Static vs Dynamic Classification: is_static_config_var() marks restart-bound parameters (such as performance_schema, innodb_log_file_size, and innodb_buffer_pool_instances) with requires_restart: true and action.type: "Config", while runtime-mutable variables emit action.type: "SQL" (SET GLOBAL ...;).
  • Sysctl and Dot-Key Filtering: Keys containing dots (Linux sysctl or Galera gcs.fc_* options) are excluded from SQL SET GLOBAL generation so agents never attempt invalid SQL assignments.
  • Deterministic Reversibility: Every finding pairs action.statement with action.rollback_statement populated from the pre-audit %myvar snapshot.

docs.text:
mysqltuner.pl drives argument parsing from a declarative %CLI_METADATA registry using Getopt::Long configured with no_auto_abbrev and no_ignore_case. Strict boundary checks reject unrecognized flags and positional arguments before any network or filesystem call occurs.

setup_environment() resolves human-readable sizing flags (--forcemem, --forceswap) via parse_human_size_to_mb(), locates basic_passwords.txt and vulnerabilities.csv, and handles offline exits (--help and --list-indicators).

docs.title: Credential Resolution and Fail-Fast Semantics
docs.text:
mysql_setup() resolves database connectivity before running OS telemetry so unreachable servers terminate cleanly:

  • Explicit Credentials: --user, --pass, --login-path, or --container attempts immediate authentication. When explicit --pass or --login-path credentials fail, report_login_failure() prints the client error (ERROR 2026 TLS hint or ERROR 2002-2005 network hint) and exits 1 without falling back to unrelated credential stores.
  • Platform Discovery: On local hosts ($doremote == 0), mysql_setup() checks Solaris svcprop, Plesk .psa.shadow, DirectAdmin mysql.conf, Debian /etc/mysql/debian.cnf, and --defaults-file before attempting ~/.my.cnf / ~/.mylogin.cnf or interactive STDIN prompting (disabled by --noask).

docs.title: Transport Abstraction (execute_system_command)
docs.text:
OS-level discovery routes through execute_system_command(), which consults get_transport_prefix() (get_ssh_prefix() first, then get_container_prefix()):

  • Shell Isolation: Remote commands are wrapped in single-quoted remote shells with embedded single quotes escaped ([REQ-INFRA-02]), while SQL statements passed through select_array() and select_one() escape double quotes, backticks, and dollar signs ([REQ-INFRA-01]).
  • Environment Awareness: In container mode (is_docker() or --container), os_setup() reads cgroup v1/v2 memory ceilings (detect_cgroup_memory_limits()) and system_recommendations() suppresses host kernel, process, and network probes that reflect the underlying container host rather than the database allocation.
  • Windows Telemetry: On $^O eq 'MSWin32', os_setup() and check_architecture() invoke PowerShell Get-CimInstance first and fall back to legacy wmic only when CIM output is missing or non-numeric.

docs.title: Metric Computation, Diagnostics, and Serialization
docs.text:
• Snapshot Acquisition: get_all_vars() executes SELECT VERSION() (with 3 connection retries), loads SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES and SHOW GLOBAL STATUS into %myvar and %mystat, checks user privileges, and adjusts Aborted_connects using the symlink-protected state file from adjust_aborted_connects().
  • Derived Calculations: calculations() verifies Questions >= 1 (exiting 2 on idle servers), delegates pure buffer/memory/traffic/cache math to helper subroutines, and computes InnoDB and binlog ratios.
  • Sectional Audits: The main loop executes all 34 subroutines in @REPORT_SECTION_NAMES (or a validated comma list via --feature), feeding @generalrec, @adjvars, @secrec, @sysrec, and @modeling.
  • Output Rendering: dump_result() writes optional standalone HTML (--reportfile), credential-redacted JSON (--json / --prettyjson via Core JSON::PP), YAML (--yaml), or AI remediation JSON (--agent-json).

docs.title: Weighted Health Score Model and Engine Version Rift
docs.text: Analytical deep dive into MySQLTuner's 40 / 30 / 30 composite health scoring model and its version-disambiguation architecture across MySQL (5.7–9.x / 26.10) and MariaDB (10.x–13.0).

docs.title: Weighted Health Score (40 / 30 / 30) Analytical Model
docs.text:
Single-metric alerts fail to convey overall server posture when a database has healthy memory ratios alongside exposed authentication risks or broken replication threads. calculate_health_score() aggregates operational telemetry into a bounded 0–100 index across three weighted pillars:

flowchart LR
    Total["WeightedHealthScore (0-100)"] --> Perf["Performance (40 pts)"]
    Total --> Sec["Security (30 pts)"]
    Total --> Res["Resilience (30 pts)"]
    Perf --> P1["perf_bp (10)"]
    Perf --> P2["perf_temp (10)"]
    Perf --> P3["perf_thread (10)"]
    Perf --> P4["perf_conn (10)"]
    Sec --> S1["30 - 5 * scalar(@secrec)"]
    Res --> R1["res_lag (10)"]
    Res --> R2["res_logs (10)"]
    Res --> R3["res_meta (10)"]

docs.title: Design Mechanics and Neutral Fallbacks
docs.text:
• Performance (40 points): Four orthogonal indicators (perf_bp, perf_temp, perf_thread, perf_conn) each contribute 0, 5, or 10 points (perf_conn is binary 10 below 80% and 0 at or above 80%). When a metric is undefined (for instance, an unexercised cache), calculate_health_score() assigns a neutral 5 points rather than penalizing an inactive feature with 0.
  • Security (30 points): Starts at 30 and subtracts 5 points per entry pushed onto @secrec (covering unencrypted sessions, disabled TLS, insecure TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 or weak ciphers, anonymous users, empty passwords, and deprecated authentication plugins), floored at 0.
  • Resilience (30 points): Combines replication health (res_lag: 10 pts standalone or < 1s lag, 5 pts for 1..59s, 0 pts for stopped threads or >= 60s), redo/binlog sizing stability (res_logs: -5 pts if innodb_log_file_size or innodb_redo_log_capacity needs tuning), and schema modeling health (res_meta: -5 pts when scalar(@modeling) > 5).
  • Complementary KPIs: Alongside the composite WeightedHealthScore, calculate_sectional_health_scores() emits five independent 0–100 domain scores (General, Storage, Security, Replication, Modeling) and a ResourceSaturation vector (CPU, Memory, Connections, IO) so high performance scores cannot mask localized saturation.

docs.title: MySQL vs MariaDB Version Rift Analysis
docs.text: MySQL and MariaDB diverged substantially after MySQL 5.7 and MariaDB 10.0, making naive major.minor version checks unsafe when a single script targets both ecosystems.

docs.title: Authoritative Engine Disambiguation (is_mariadb())
docs.text:
Historically, calculations() stripped vendor suffixes from $myvar{'version'} (s/(.+)-.*?$/$1/) after storing the original string in $real_vars{'version'}. Once MySQL introduced calendar-style releases (26.7, 26.10) alongside MariaDB 10.x–13.0, checking major >= 10 alone misclassified MySQL 26.x as MariaDB.

is_mariadb() resolves this ambiguity in three deterministic stages:

  1. Match mariadb case-insensitively in $myvar{'version'} or $myvar{'version_comment'} (returning 1), or match mysql|percona|oracle|aurora (returning 0).
  2. Compare the unstripped $real_vars{'version'} base prefix when -MariaDB was stripped during calculations().
  3. Fall back to numeric major bounds ( $maj >= 10 && $maj < 26 ), which isolates MariaDB 10.x–13.x from MySQL 5.5–9.x and 26.x.

docs.text: Subsystem MySQL (5.7–9.x / 26.10) MariaDB (10.x–13.0) Diagnostic Adaptation Replication Commands SHOW REPLICA STATUS (>= 8.0.22); SHOW SLAVE STATUS (< 8.0.22) SHOW REPLICA STATUS (>= 10.5); SHOW SLAVE STATUS (< 10.5) Probes REPLICA variables and falls back to SLAVE equivalents User Auth Store mysql.user (authentication_string), PASSWORD() removed in 8.0+ mysql.global_priv JSON (Priv column) in 10.4+ Queries JSON_VALUE(Priv, '$.plugin') on MariaDB 10.4+; uses Perl Digest::SHA offline Auth Migration Target Recommends caching_sha2_password (mysql_native_password removed in 9.0) Recommends ed25519, parsec, or unix_socket check_auth_plugins() branches on $is_mariadb and 8.0/8.4/9.0 TLS Availability Signal have_ssl removed in 8.4+; falls back to Ssl_cipher and performance_schema.tls_channel_status have_ssl; 11.4+ supports zero-configuration TLS without explicit ssl_cert/ssl_key get_server_tls_status() checks multi-signal fallback; skips cert warning on MariaDB 11.4+ auto-TLS InnoDB Redo & BP innodb_redo_log_capacity replaces innodb_log_file_size in 8.0.30+ Retains innodb_log_file_size; removes innodb_buffer_pool_instances (10.4+) and autosizes chunk (10.8+) Guards instance checks with !(is_mariadb() && >= 10.4) and skips chunk 0 on MariaDB 10.8+ Query Cache & Variables Query cache removed in 8.0; tx_isolation removed in 8.0 Query cache retained (Com_select includes Qcache_hits); tx_isolation deprecated 11.1+ audit_deprecated_variables() checks GLOBAL_VALUE_ORIGIN so default MariaDB aliases do not false-positive

docs.title: ADR-001: Single-File Perl and Zero-Dependency Core Architecture
docs.text: Attribute Value Status Accepted Date 2026-11-23 Deciders Project Maintainers (Constitution Tier 00) Supersedes None

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Database administrators frequently execute diagnostic tooling on hardened, air-gapped, or ephemeral Linux, BSD, Solaris, AIX, macOS, and Windows hosts where installing compilers, CPAN toolchains, or third-party runtime packages is prohibited or impractical.

MySQLTuner's core mission requires a tool that can be copied as a single artifact onto any target host and audited directly by security teams before execution.

docs.title: Options Considered and Trade-Offs
docs.text: Option Deployment Friction Security Auditability Maintenance Ergonomics Verdict Option A: Single-file mysqltuner.pl + Perl Core modules only Minimal (wget or scp one file; runs on base Perl) High (entire engine in one inspectable file) Medium (requires strict sectioning and perltidy) Selected Option B: Multi-file Perl package (lib/*.pm + CPAN DBI/DBD::mysql) High (requires CPAN, C headers, or OS package manager) Medium (dependency tree expands attack surface) High (modular files) Rejected Option C: Compiled binary (Go/Rust) or Python package Medium-High (cross-arch builds or Python venv needed) Medium High Rejected for core engine

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Adopt Option A as an immutable constitutional constraint for mysqltuner.pl:

  1. Keep the entire diagnostic engine inside a single executable file (mysqltuner.pl). Splitting mysqltuner.pl into external .pm modules is prohibited.
  2. Restrict imports strictly to Perl Core modules (POSIX, File::Spec, File::Temp, Getopt::Long, Pod::Usage, Sys::Hostname, File::Basename, Cwd) and graceful eval { require ... } checks for optional Core modules (JSON::PP, Time::HiRes, Digest::SHA, Time::Local).
  3. Delegate SQL execution through existing mysql / mariadb and mysqladmin / mariadb-admin CLI binaries rather than requiring DBD::mysql or DBD::MariaDB.
  4. Isolate optional ecosystem microservices (such as build/mcp_server.py) as external wrappers using Python 3 standard library only, leaving the core Perl diagnostic tool self-contained.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Zero-Install Portability: Administrators can download or copy mysqltuner.pl directly into air-gapped environments and run diagnostics immediately using base Perl.
  • Minimal Attack Surface: Excluding third-party CPAN modules eliminates external supply-chain dependencies and simplifies security sign-off.
  • Transport Uniformity: Invoking mysql and OS utilities through execute_system_command() enables identical execution locally, over SSH (--ssh-host), or inside containers (--container).

docs.title: Negative and Structural Mitigations
docs.text:
• Large Single-File Footprint: mysqltuner.pl exceeds 19,000 lines, raising merge-conflict and readability risks. The project mitigates this by enforcing perltidy formatting, pure calculation helper functions, automated compliance auditing (build/check_compliance.pl), and subtest-decomposed unit tests in tests/.
  • CLI Subprocess Parsing: Querying via the mysql CLI rather than a binary wire driver requires defensive shell escaping (_shell_quote(), [REQ-INFRA-01], [REQ-INFRA-02]) and explicit client error extraction (extract_client_error()).

docs.title: ADR-002: Versioned Diátaxis Documentation Architecture
docs.text: Attribute Value Status Accepted Date 2026-11-23 Deciders Project Maintainers Supersedes Legacy PHP documentation site and ad-hoc root Markdown cross-links

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
MySQLTuner documentation historically spanned root-level generated Markdown (USAGE.md, FEATURES.md, mysql_support.md, mariadb_support.md, SECURITY.md), historical release notes (releases/v*.md), multilingual READMEs, and architectural specifications under documentation/, alongside a legacy PHP website.

Keeping operator runbooks, conceptual architecture, and CLI reference tables synchronized across releases required a static, version-aware publishing pipeline deployable to https://mysqltuner.lightpath.fr/ on IONOS SFTP hosting.

docs.title: Options Considered and Trade-Offs
docs.text: Option Genre Clarity Release Versioning Shared Hosting Compatibility (IONOS SFTP) Verdict Option A: Diátaxis 4-quadrant docs/ + MkDocs Material + mike (alias_type: redirect) High (enforced by CI gates) Native (latest, vX.Y.Z, dev) High (pure static HTML/JS/CSS + .htaccess) Selected Option B: Legacy static PHP site with manual HTML updates Low (mixed prose and snippets) Manual directory copies Requires PHP runtime and manual routing Rejected Option C: MkDocs Material + mike with alias_type: symlink High Native Low (SFTP deploys and Apache FollowSymLinks often fail on shared hosts) Rejected

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Adopt Option A:

  1. Diátaxis 4-Quadrant Tree: Organize user and contributor documentation under docs/ into 01-tutorials/, 02-how-to-guides/, 03-reference/, and 04-explanation/, keeping 02-how-to-guides/ compliant with ASD-STE100 Issue 9 procedural clarity.
  2. Build-Time Single-Source Reuse (build/mkdocs_hooks.py): Keep canonical generated files (USAGE.md, FEATURES.md, mysql_support.md, mariadb_support.md, SECURITY.md, CURRENT_VERSION.txt, and releases/v*.md) in the repository root and inject them dynamically at build time via <!-- INCLUDE_SOURCE: ... -->, <!-- CURRENT_VERSION -->, and <!-- AUTO_RELEASES_TABLE -->.
  3. Versioned Hosting via mike Redirects: Publish immutable vX.Y.Z snapshots, latest, and dev channels to the docs-site branch using alias_type: redirect and canonical_version: latest (never symlink), then synchronize the archived tree plus build/docs_htaccess to IONOS over SFTP.
  4. Docs-as-Code CI Gates: Enforce build/check_diataxis_docs.py docs --strict, markdownlint-cli2, mkdocs build --strict, and tests/unit_mkdocs_diataxis.t on pull requests.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Single Source of Truth: Generated root files (USAGE.md, FEATURES.md, *_support.md, releases/v*.md) remain the authoritative data inputs without manual copy-paste drift inside docs/.
  • Clean Static Security Posture: Replacing dynamic PHP scripts with static HTML, .htaccess security headers, and no-cache headers on versions.json removes server-side execution surface.
  • Strict Genre Separation: Operators find 1-action runbooks in 02-how-to-guides/ while engineers consult specifications in 03-reference/ and ADRs in 04-explanation/.

docs.title: Negative and Operational Mitigations
docs.text:
• Dual Documentation Trees: Legacy contributor specifications in documentation/ remain outside docs/ so existing audit scripts (build/check_doc_links.pl, build/audit_specifications.pl) continue passing uninterrupted.
  • SFTP Credential Dependency: Automated publishing requires IONOS_FTP_SERVER, IONOS_FTP_USERNAME, IONOS_FTP_PASSWORD, and IONOS_REMOTE_PATH secrets; workflows degrade gracefully to docs-site branch builds when secrets are absent or dry_run is selected.
